title: Scene
description: A contiguous range of paragraphs, in reading order, with one place, one story time and one cast. A scene may cross a chapter boundary. Scenes never overlap; they need not cover every paragraph. The support cites the paragraphs that mark the scene's boundaries.

end.description: Last paragraph of the scene, inclusive. Equal to or after `start`.

place.description: Where the scene happens: an entity of kind `place`. Absent when the producer cannot tell.

time.description: When the scene happens in the story.

label.description: Story time in words, in the book's language, as a reader would say it.

date.description: Calendar date, as precise as the text allows: `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD` (negative years allowed).

story_order.description: Position of the scene in story (fabula) order, 1 = earliest. Scenes may share a value when the order between them is unknown. Comparing it with reading order shows the anachronies (Genette's order).

setting.description: The frame that holds over the scene (where, when, on which plane, in whose voice, how it is told, weather, light, company), with its own support. Paragraph-level detail goes in the layer's setting spans.

continues.description: Id of an earlier scene this one resumes after an interruption (same place, time and cast, broken by other text).
